draft.title: Egypt's social pyramid
card: Ancient Egyptian society was layered like a pyramid. Few people were at the top and most were at the bottom.
The pharaoh ruled at the top. Below came viziers (the pharaoh's chief officials), priests and nobles.
Next came scribes, who could read and write, and craftworkers. Farmers and slaves were at the bottom, and farmers were the largest group.
Women could own property, such as land and goods, even though men held most top jobs.
draft.remember: Few held power at the top. Most people farmed or served at the bottom.

a.q: Which group was at the very top of Egypt's social pyramid?
opts: The pharaoh
The viziers
The priests
The nobles
a.why: The pharaoh ruled over everyone else. Viziers were powerful officials, but they served the pharaoh and ranked below him.

b.q: Neferu lives in Egypt and reads and writes records for a noble. Where does she fit on the social pyramid?
opts: In the middle, among the scribes
At the top, among the viziers
At the bottom, among the farmers
At the top, beside the pharaoh
b.why: Scribes could read and write, and they sat below the nobles and above farmers. Viziers were top officials just below the pharaoh, so a scribe working for a noble is not one of them.
b.clue: Which group was known for reading and writing?

b.best: In the middle, among the scribes

problems.detail: The scenario makes Neferu, a woman, a scribe. Almost all ancient Egyptian scribes were men and female scribes were very rare. Presenting a female scribe as ordinary could give students a false picture, especially since the card says men held most top jobs. A male name, or a note that this was unusual, would avoid this.

check.summary: Both questions have one clear right answer, and the card and explanations are accurate. The only issue is that question b's scribe is a woman, which was very rare in ancient Egypt and could mislead students.
